shared_elements: carved stone surface in low relief
prominent circle/disc motif on the upper-central area
horizontal band(s) dividing the surface into zones
broadly symmetrical composition about a vertical axis
rounded upper contour of the stone
justification: Both are upright stone monuments with a symmetrical, vertically axial layout that includes a conspicuous disc in the upper-middle zone and horizontal dividing bands below, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they differ fundamentally: A is a massive three-dimensional block whose carving wraps a body-like volume in heavily weathered, bold rounded forms, while B is a thin flat slab with crisp, shallow linear incision organised into a framed scene of two flanking figures.
